summary: Ernst Gustaf Ferdinand Olbers was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. from Lund University (1856–1862). He served as principal at Högre lärarinneseminariet from 1868 to 1879.

Indologist Ernst Haas studied at Berlin under Albrecht Weber, Bonn, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth (Ph.D.). He served as Keeper of Oriental Printed Books and Manuscripts at the British Museum (1866) and Professor of Sanskrit at University College London (1875).
Ernst Haeckel studied at the Humboldt University of Berlin and Frederick William University Berlin (~1854–1857). He later served at the University of Jena from circa 1862 to 1909.

Ernst Heinrich Meier was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Jena, Göttingen, and Tübingen under Heinrich Ewald (Ph.D.). He spent his career at the University of Tübingen, serving as Privatdozent (1841), extraordinary professor (1848), and ordinary professor (1856).

Ernst Johann Eitel worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Maulbronn, Blaubeuren, Esslingen, and the University of Tübingen (M.A. ~1856–1860, Ph.D. ~1870–1871), he was appointed Lecturer in German at the University of Adelaide in 1898.

Ernst Kalinka, a scholar in history and archaeology, studied at the University of Vienna (~1884–1889). He subsequently held posts at Chernivtsi University (~1900–1903) and the University of Innsbruck (~1903–1934).

Indologist and linguist Ernst Kuhn studied in Berlin, Halle, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Halle (1871) and Leipzig (1872–1875) before becoming ordinary professor at Heidelberg (1875–1877) and Munich (1877–1917).

Indologist and linguist Ernst Leumann studied at Zurich, Geneva, Berlin, and Leipzig under Ernst Windisch (Ph.D. 1878–1881). He served as professor at the University of Strasbourg (1884–1919) and honorary professor at the University of Freiburg (1919).

Linguist and Indologist Ernst Lewy studied at Breslau (Ph.D.), Munich, Leipzig, and Berlin, under Alfred Hillebrandt and Franz Nikolaus Finck. He served as professor of Hungarian at Berlin (1925–1935), worked at the Royal Irish Academy, and held a chair at UCD.

Ernst Moritz Arndt was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the universities of Greifswald (~1791–1793) and Jena (~1793–1794). He later held academic posts at Greifswald (~1800–1811) and Bonn (~1818–1860).

Linguist Ernst Moritz Ludwig Ettmüller studied under Bernhard Hirzel and attended the universities of Leipzig (~1823–1826) and Jena (~1826–1828). He later held posts at the University of Jena (~1828–1833) and the University of Zurich (~1833–1877).

Indologist and linguist Ernst Osiander attended the seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren and studied at the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth (Dr. phil. 1847–1853). He served as Repetent at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren (~1852–1854) and the Tübinger Stift (1857–1860).

Linguist and Indologist Ernst Otto August Heuman earned his fil.kand. at Uppsala University. He worked for the Santal Mission, served as school principal and head of the Church of Sweden Mission, and became Bishop of the Tamil Evangelical Lutheran Church in 1921.
Ernst Philipp Ludwig Calmberg, active in Indology, studied at the University of Jena, earning a Lic. theol. by 1830. He served as a teacher at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums beginning in 1819.
Ernst Prets is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held posts attested at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1995–1996) and at the University of Vienna (1996).

Linguist and Indologist Ernst Risch studied under Manu Leumann at Zurich (Ph.D. 1930–1935) and Ferdinand Sommer at Munich. He spent his career at the University of Zurich as PD (1942), Titularprofessor (1950), extraordinary professor (1956), and ordinary professor (1959–1981).

Sinologist and Indologist Ernst Schierlitz studied at the University of Munich under Lucian Scherman and Wilhelm Geiger (Ph.D. ~1921–1926). He worked at the Bavarian State Library, directed the Deutschland-Institut (~1930–1935), and served as librarian at Fu Jen Catholic University (1930–1938).

Linguist Ernst Schwarz studied at the German University in Prague's philosophy faculty (~1914–1920) and the Deutsche wissenschaftliche Prüfungs-kommission in Prague. He later held a post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1955–1963).

Ernst Schäfer worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology, studying at Göttingen and Berlin under Erwin Stresemann (Ph.D.). He served as PD at Munich (1942), professor at the Central University of Venezuela (1949–1954), and curator at the Lower Saxony State Museum (1960–1970).

Ernst Siecke, active in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies, earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin (1864–1869), studying under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He taught at the Lessing-Gymnasium from circa 1878 to 1911 as schoolteacher and professor.
